source_text: We conclude that a mix of evolution-based adaptive forest management, assisted migration, and long-term breeding programs will be required to achieve mitigation of the effects of climate change on European forests.

We suggest that management options should have the following three characteristics: being predictive, that is, taking advantage of currently available models to predict the fate of forests under climate change and management options; being integrative, that is, taking into account multiple aspects of vulnerability; being locally optimised, that is, being tailored to individual Genetic Conservation Units and to their specific conservation needs.

While assisted migration is one option, fostering the maintenance of functional diversity within forest stands – however this is best achieved locally – is an equally valuable (and not mutually exclusive) option to consider, particularly for those forests that showed high levels of vulnerability.
We suggest that in situ protection of these populations should be the norm and ex situ the back up.

The conservation and management of forest genetic resources must take into account multiple risk factors, leading to levels of vulnerability that can vary across species and across ecological zones within a given species.

Η δημιουργία των μελλοντικών σεναρίων είναι η τελευταία σε μια σειρά από δράσεις όπως η αξιολόγηση παρελθουσών αναγκών και προσδοκιών, ο ορισμός του συνόλου των φορέων αλλαγής (drivers of change) σε σχέση με την χρήση ψηφιακών εργαλείων στις αγροτικές δραστηριότητες.
Η αποτύπωση αυτή ήταν το πρώτο και βασικό βήμα για να ξεδιπλωθούν όλες οι προαναφερθείσες δράσεις του ΖΕ.
Η ανάπτυξη των ψηφιακών δεξιοτήτων των καλλιεργητών είναι θεμελιώδης παράγοντας για επαρκή ανταπόκριση στις τεχνικές απαιτήσεις της ‘ψηφιακής’ γεωργίας.
